signals.title: AUD/USD — Employment Shock + Positioning Squeeze
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6957, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.7010/0.7088/0.7044 following a severe domestic labor market miss. September employment fell by 39.3k against expectations for a 14.0k gain, while the unemployment rate ticked up to 4.7% (z=+2.45σ shock per ESI surprise data). This labor contraction rapidly diminishes near-term RBA tightening expectations, leaving leveraged specs exposed. Leveraged funds hold +48,911 net long contracts (70.3% long), having reduced positions by 6,203 contracts WoW. While the 60bp cash rate advantage favors AUD (RBA 4.60% vs Fed 4.00%), speculative positioning faces swift unwinding risk if the yield premium erodes. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, vulnerable to speculative long liquidation. Catalyst: RBA meeting 3 Nov — hold bias. Risk: Rapid recovery back above the 200-day moving average at 0.7044 negates the downside breakdown.

signals.title: NOK/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: NOK leads the weekly G10 currency performance with an average gain of +0.733% across 2 pairs, while USD lags at -0.166% across 9 pairs, generating a significant 0.899% bilateral spread. Norges Bank policy rate at 4.50% carries a +1.82% real rate stance compared to Fed 4.00% carrying a +1.67% real rate stance. Spot USD/NOK trades below its SMA20 (9.528) and SMA200 (9.539) at 9.512, establishing a bearish structural track. Retail positioning displays an extreme 95% long exposure on USD/NOK, presenting a textbook contrarian setup against the prevailing macro trend. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK, contrarian to retail extreme. Catalyst: Norges Bank meeting 5 Nov — hold bias. Risk: USD/NOK reclaiming the 200-day moving average at 9.539 invalidates the downward extension.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Hedging vs Carry Resilience
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.94, anchored above its SMA20 (157.75) and SMA50 (157.72) while capped under the SMA200 at 158.55. Saxo Bank 25d risk reversals print at -1.70, highlighting a heavy put skew and aggressive downside hedging among institutional participants. Conversely, 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 7.6% against a 30-day realized volatility of 9.5%, yielding a negative volatility risk premium of -1.9%. The underlying 275bp rate spread (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%; SOFR-TONA spread at +266bp) continues to support carry flows while VIX remains contained at 16.9. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY on dips, supported by carry while 157.70 holds. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 30 Oct — hold bias. Risk: A daily close below the SMA50 at 157.72 triggers broader options delta hedging toward 156.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Shorts + Technical Compression
signals.text: EUR/USD sits at 1.1218, pinned below its descending SMA20 (1.1312), SMA50 (1.1484), and SMA200 (1.1592). CFTC data shows leveraged funds holding -84,775 net short contracts (34.4% long) at the 4th percentile of the 52-week range (z=-1.64), reflecting stretched short positioning. The 135bp policy rate premium favors the greenback (Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65%), with OIS spreads running +145bp in USD's favor. However, the BEER fair value model flags EUR/USD as undervalued at z=-2.23σ against a model equilibrium of 1.1331. Trade bias: Neutral/range EUR/USD, downside capped by crowded speculative shorts. Catalyst: Eurozone CPI release at 09:00 UTC. Risk: A downside break below 1.1150 resumes the broader macro downtrend toward 1.1080.
